title: Niche model snapshot probe and seller-sentiment sensor
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Run a lightweight, repeatable probe that captures short snapshots of narrow-domain open models (specialty medical, legal, regulatory) and couples model behavior signals with public seller / vendor sentiment. Goal: early detection of emerging models that are high-risk/high-opportunity for Redwood customers and identify seller confidence and survivability signals that should feed the Model Watchtower. The probe will: 1) define 6 representative micro-prompts per domain (3 deterministic, 3 adversarial), 2) automate weekly scoring across a rotating set of candidate models, 3) extract signal metrics (latency, hallucination risk proxies, safety flags, token cost, deterministic divergence), and 4) crosslink each model snapshot to seller health signals (GitHub activity, release cadence, job postings, vendor tweets, forum threads). Deliverables: weekly snapshot CSV, signal ingestion into the sentinel pipeline, and a short playbook for triaging models that cross trigger thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: 6 micro-prompts per target domain committed and reviewed in the repo
Automated weekly job that runs probes against 12 candidate models with results stored in S3/drive
Signal extraction pipeline maps at least 8 metrics per run and pushes to the Model Watchtower ingestion endpoint
Seller-sentiment enrichment (GitHub/Slack/Twitter/forum indicators) attached to each model record
Playbook with triage thresholds and owner rotation published to Confluence

notes: We purposely limit scope to snapshot probes (not full benchmarks) to keep costs low and cadence high.
Seller-sentiment signals are heuristics (activity cadence, release velocity, recruiter postings); we will quantify reliability over 6 weeks.
If a model crosses hallucination and divergence thresholds AND seller sentiment degrades, it should trigger a canary-run and procurement alert.
